Greptile Summary

This PR lets recovery authentication codes be created and read through user storage. The main changes are: - Added a shared helper for recovery-code creation with user-storage fallback. - Added federated-first recovery-code lookup for login. - Extended the backwards-compatibility user-storage provider and tests for recovery codes.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Recovery-code reset and replay paths can leave old or reused codes valid. - User-storage creation can skip cleanup of existing stored recovery codes. - Federated credential lookup can parse metadata-only credentials as full recovery-code secrets. - The test provider accepts a matching recovery code without consuming it. CredentialHelper.java, RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java, and BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java

Security Review

 Recovery-code resets can leave older codes valid, and the user-storage validation path can allow replay of the same recovery code. Both affect the single-use guarantee for backup authentication codes.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds client resources to the admin authorization schema. The main changes are: - A new `Clients` resource type and client-specific scopes. - A V2 client permission evaluator wired through `MgmtPermissionsV2`. - Tests for client manage, view, configure, and role-mapping permissions. - Shared test helpers for user and client permission setup.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The client authorization path can evaluate the wrong resource, and client-removal cleanup can throw under V2. - Client permission lookups use an owner id that does not match resource creation. - Per-client resources can skip all-client resource-type policies. - Client listing can miss users' client-specific grants. - Client deletion can hit an unsupported V2 cleanup method. ClientPermissionsV2.java, AdminPermissionsSchema.java, AdminPermissions.java

Security Review

 The changed client authorization path can skip or misread client permission resources. This can make client grants or denies apply incorrectly under V2.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds configurable worker processes for span buffer flushing. The main changes are: - Adds a `--flusher-processes` option for `process-spans`. - Splits assigned Redis shards across flusher workers. - Tracks flusher health, backpressure, and memory checks per worker. - Updates span flusher tests for the new worker layout.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The worker lifecycle and new CLI parsing path need fixes before merging. - Invalid `--flusher-processes` values can crash consumer startup. - Restarted workers can leave killed child processes unreaped. - Timed joins can leave later workers running after shutdown returns. - The Redis memory check repeats the same cluster-wide query per worker. src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py; src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py

**Shutdown Stops Before Drain** `shutdown()` sets each worker's stop flag before the queues are drained. A worker that processes one item after `Queue.shutdown(immediate=False)` will exit on the next loop check, leaving later queued items unprocessed when the pool shutdown returns.

**Final Worker Commits Are Lost** `close()` stops the commit thread before shutting down the worker pool. Any offsets completed while workers finish during `queue_pool.shutdown()` have no later commit pass, so already-processed messages can be redelivered after a graceful shutdown or rebalance.

**Factory Reuses Closed Pool** The factory creates one `FixedQueuePool`, but each `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` shuts that pool down. If the same factory instance creates another strategy after a close or rebalance, later submissions can target queues whose workers are already stopped, and the submit exception path can mark those messages complete without processing.

**Redis Key Type Changes In Place** The same `span-buf:s:{...}` keys that were previously written with `SADD` are now written with `ZADD`, and the Lua/flusher paths now use sorted-set commands on them. **Redirect Chain Splits Earlier** The redirect traversal cap drops from 10000 to 1000 without an overflow path. A trace whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 hops stops at an intermediate set id, so later spans can be linked into the wrong partial tree and the final trace can flush as orphaned segments. ```suggestion for i = 0, 10000 do local new_set_span = redis.call("hget", main_redirect_key, set_span_id) ```

**Configured Span Limit Is Ignored** Eviction is now hard-coded to 1000 spans in Lua, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` is no longer enforced during flush. Any deployment or test that constructs the buffer with a different span limit will still evict at 1000, so segments can be truncated too early or allowed past the configured cap.

Greptile Summary

This PR changes audit-log pagination and span buffering. The main changes are: - Adds an optimized audit-log paginator behind a query parameter. - Stores buffered spans in Redis sorted sets scored by end timestamp. - Evicts large span buffers during insertion. - Updates span processing and tests to include `end_timestamp_precise`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The GitHub setup validation path needs fixes before merging. - Reinstalling a disabled GitHub integration can stop at the invalid-installation page instead of reactivating the integration. - Existing integrations without `sender` metadata can return a server error during validation. - The main OAuth flow and mismatch case are covered by tests. src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py

The main changes are: - `InstrumentationMiddleware` becomes `MetricsMiddleware`. - Contextual plugin log fields move into `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`. - `LoggerMiddleware` now reads contextual fields through `Logger.FromContext`. - The plugin middleware stack now inserts metrics, contextual logging, and request logging as separate layers.

Default upgrades can fail during the embedding-host migration, and migrated hosts can stop authorizing embeds. - The migration reads missing legacy setting rows before checking for fallback values. - Legacy host strings are inserted without the normalization used by the new lookup. - Accepted port-specific hosts cannot match incoming referers. - Shared REST hydration can drop relationship ids when side-loaded records are absent. db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, app/models/embeddable_host.rb, app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6

An allowed article URL can redirect to an internal host such as metadata or admin services, so the server still performs the internal request even though the original URL matched `embeddable_host`.

**Remote Fetcher Not Loaded** `import_remote` uses `open(url).read`, but this file does not require `open-uri` and callers such as `TopicRetriever` and the Disqus task do not load it first. In those paths, fetching an HTTP article can fail at runtime instead of importing the topic.

**Concurrent Imports Race** The import path checks for an existing `embed_url` and then creates the row without locking or rescuing the unique-index conflict. Two requests or a feed poll and on-demand retrieval for the same URL can both see no row; one then raises on `TopicEmbed.create!`, causing a request error or a dropped scheduled poll because the job disables retries.

**Embed Stylesheet Not Precompiled** The layout references a standalone `embed` stylesheet, but the PR does not add `embed.css` to the Rails asset precompile list. In production asset mode, the iframe can render without its stylesheet or raise an asset-not-precompiled error when the embed page loads. **Missing Slash Breaks Iframe URL** If the embed snippet sets `discourseUrl` to the common form `https://forum.example.com` without a trailing slash, this concatenation produces `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`. The iframe then navigates to the wrong host/path and the embed never loads. ```suggestion if (discourseUrl.charAt(discourseUrl.length - 1) !== '/') { discourseUrl += '/'; } iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl); ```

**Disqus Links Fetch Arbitrary Hosts** The importer now fetches `t[:link]` live through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and that value comes from the Disqus XML without scheme or host validation. A modified export can make the import task request internal HTTP services instead of importing only the expected Disqus thread content.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds credential syncing between Cal.com and self-hosted app stores. The main changes are: - A new webhook for creating and updating app credentials. - Shared helpers for synced OAuth token refreshes. - OAuth refresh wiring across several calendar and video integrations. - New environment variables for the sync secret, endpoint, and encryption key.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The synced OAuth refresh path can store broken credentials and fail token refreshes across multiple integrations. - The shared refresh helper returns a different object shape than several updated callers expect. - The token parser can persist placeholder refresh tokens and accepts responses without a usable expiry. - Salesforce and Zoho Bigin have integration-specific sync regressions that can refresh the wrong account or skip the configured sync endpoint. OAuth refresh helpers and the changed Google, Zoho Bigin, Salesforce, and webhook credential paths.

Security Review

 The new webhook is protected by a shared secret, but authenticated sync payloads are written to stored credentials without app-specific schema validation.

**Reschedule Cancel Is Not Awaited** This `try` block starts async cancellations for the original booking but does not wait for them, so async failures are not caught and the reschedule flow can continue to create the new booking. The old booking's scheduled reminders can remain active alongside the new booking's reminders. ```suggestion await Promise.all( originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.map((reminder) => { if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) { return deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true); } else if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.SMS) { return deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); } return Promise.resolve(); }) ); ```

**Edited Steps Keep Old Reminders** When a workflow step is edited, this loop starts cancellation of the reminders from the old step settings but does not wait before continuing to schedule replacements. A slow or failed cancellation can leave the old reminder scheduled, so the booking can receive both the old and new workflow reminder. ```suggestion await Promise.all( remindersToUpdate.map((reminder) => { if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) { return deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); } else if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.SMS) { return deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); } return Promise.resolve(); }) ); ```

Greptile Summary

This PR changes calendar destination handling so collective bookings can target more than one host calendar. The main changes are: - `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` now accepts an array. - Booking, payment, reminder, confirmation, cancellation, and reschedule flows wrap stored destination calendars into arrays. - Event creation now loops destination calendars and records credential/calendar ids on booking references. - Calendar providers were updated to read the new destination-calendar shape.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The multi-calendar booking path can crash or write to the wrong host calendar. - Empty destination-calendar arrays can throw in the Google Meet fallback. - Later collective hosts can be routed through the first destination calendar in non-Google providers. - Google updates can lose their calendar fallback when old references lack an external calendar id. - Recurring cancellation can repeat or mis-target external deletes with multiple calendar references. - Organization creation now stores slugs under the opposite billing flag. EventManager calendar routing, Google update fallback, recurring cancellation cleanup, and organization slug creation.
